## DISORT on CUDA by pydisort version (`solver: disort`) {#sec-ch09-disort}

### Summary

When a band runs with `solver: disort`, pyharp hands the column to pydisort, so whether DISORT can run on a GPU is
decided by the pydisort installed next to pyharp, not by pyharp. Two versions matter: 1.7.1, the version pyharp's
CI installs, and 1.8.13, the version `pip` installs for pyharp's requirement `pydisort>=1.7.1`. With 1.7.1 DISORT
cannot run on CUDA at all: the call raises. With 1.8.13 it runs and agrees with the CPU to round-off at 4, 16 and
32 streams, but not at 8 streams, and not to round-off for thermal columns with a single-scattering albedo of
one. On the CPU the two versions give bit-identical fluxes, and batching is exact in both.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Which DISORT operations run on CUDA, per pydisort version, and how close they come to the CPU.

**Data.** Properties (nwave, ncol, nlyr, 2 + nmom); fluxes (nwave, ncol, nlyr + 1, 2).

**Placement.** Inside `DisortImpl::forward`, called by `RadiationBandImpl::forward`.

**Activation.** `solver: disort`; device and precision of the inputs. Default CPU.

**Guarantee / limits.** 1.7.1: no CUDA. 1.8.13: round-off except at `nstr`[^rg-7bd767bf2209] 8 and thermal $\omega = 1$.

**Evidence.** See the Tests layer below.
:::

Local symbols: $\mathrm{nd}$ as in @eq-ch09-toon-nd; $\delta\omega_{\mathrm{D}}$ the margin cdisort subtracts from a
single-scattering albedo of one [-].

### Derivation

**Why a DISORT batch equals a loop over columns.** pydisort keeps one cdisort state per (wavelength, column) pair and
runs the column solver `c_disort` once per element of a tensor iterator, with no step across elements:
`DisortImpl::forward` builds the iterator ({{< code src/disort.cpp DisortImpl::forward repo=pydisort >}}) and the
CPU driver `call_disort_cpu` loops over its elements ({{< code src/disort_dispatch.cpp call_disort_cpu repo=pydisort >}}).
The argument is that of @sec-ch09-toon, Derivation, and gives $\mathrm{nd} = 0$ between a batch and a loop.

**Why columns with $\omega = 1$ need a looser tolerance.** cdisort does not solve a conservative layer as such; it
moves the single-scattering albedo off one,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\delta\omega_{\mathrm{D}} &= 100\,\epsilon_{\mathrm{mach}} \\
\omega &\leftarrow 1 - \delta\omega_{\mathrm{D}} ,
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch09-disort-dither}
<!-- equation-check: eq-ch09-disort-dither check_ch09_batch_device.py -->
<!-- equation-source: eq-ch09-disort-dither cdisort's treatment of a single-scattering albedo of one -->

with $\epsilon_{\mathrm{mach}}$ the double-precision machine epsilon. @eq-ch09-disort-dither is applied in `c_disort`
({{< code cdisort213/cdisort.c c_disort repo=pydisort >}}). Near $\omega = 1$ the solution changes fast with
$\omega$: the eigenvalues of the homogeneous solution approach zero, so the round-off of the two devices is amplified
far more than for $\omega < 1$. The comparison therefore holds those columns to $10^{-9}$ in float64, and the others
to the $10^{-12}$ of @sec-ch09-toon.

**What decides CUDA support.** A call on CUDA tensors reaches pydisort's dispatch stub, which has a CUDA entry only
if the installed pydisort library contains one. At the pydisort pin the CUDA driver `call_disort_cuda` is
registered in the source, but the line that would call the column solver is commented out
({{< code src/disort_dispatch.cu call_disort_cuda repo=pydisort >}}); the 1.7.1 wheel ships no CUDA library at
all. A source build of that version with CUDA would therefore return fluxes the kernel never wrote; that is read
from the code, not measured.

What is exact and what is approximate: batch against loop is exact; CUDA against CPU is round-off where the two
devices run the same solver. The check is `check_ch09_batch_device.py` (Tests layer).

### Numerical method

The inputs are 3 wavelengths $\times$ 32 columns $\times$ 20 layers, drawn as in @sec-ch09-toon, with the
single-scattering albedo set to one in every layer of columns 0 to 3. Each comparison runs at 4, 8, 16 and 32
streams with Henyey-Greenstein moments $\chi_l = g^l$, shortwave (flags `lamber,quiet,onlyfl`) and thermal (adding
`planck`), in float64 and float32. The DISORT object is configured by `disort_config`
({{< code python/disort.py disort_config repo=pyharp >}}). The same comparison is made for DISORT inside a
`RadiationBand`, built from `tests/rayleigh_test.yaml` with 8 streams and 4 columns and moved with `.cuda()`; the
band clamps $\omega$ to $1 - 10^{-12}$ before the solver ({{< code src/radiation/radiation_band.cpp RadiationBandImpl::forward repo=pyharp >}}).

```{python}

#| fig-cap: "Support matrix: for each solver (rows) and operation (columns: batch against single columns on the CPU, CUDA against CPU, in float64 and float32), the state under pydisort 1.7.1 (left) and 1.8.13 (right). Green 'pass': within the tolerance; vermillion 'fail': a candidate defect described in Limits; hatched 'none': the call raises because the installed pydisort has no CUDA kernel; white 'n/a': not measured. Toon is the same under both versions; DISORT on CUDA is impossible with 1.7.1 and partly wrong with 1.8.13."
#| fig-alt: "Two grids of five rows and four columns. Left grid, pydisort 1.7.1: Toon rows all pass; DISORT rows pass for batch and say none for CUDA; band row says n/a for batch and none for CUDA. Right grid, pydisort 1.8.13: Toon rows all pass; DISORT rows pass for batch and fail for CUDA; band row n/a for batch and pass for CUDA."
```

### Code

@tbl-ch09-disort-code lists the code at the pydisort pin that decides batching and CUDA support.

| what | code link | symbol | switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| iterator over (wavelength, column) | {{< code src/disort.cpp DisortImpl::forward repo=pydisort >}} | `DisortImpl::forward` | `solver: disort` |
| CPU driver | {{< code src/disort_dispatch.cpp call_disort_cpu repo=pydisort >}} | `call_disort_cpu` | CPU inputs |
| CUDA driver (body commented out) | {{< code src/disort_dispatch.cu call_disort_cuda repo=pydisort >}} | `call_disort_cuda` | CUDA inputs |
| $\omega$ margin of the band | {{< code src/radiation/radiation_band.cpp RadiationBandImpl::forward repo=pyharp >}} | `RadiationBandImpl::forward` | always in a band |

: Code map of DISORT batching and dispatch. {#tbl-ch09-disort-code}

1. `RadiationBandImpl::forward` assembles the properties, clamps $\omega \le 1 - \delta\omega$ with
   $\delta\omega = 10^{-12}$ (float64) or $10^{-6}$ (float32), and calls the band's solver
   ({{< code src/radiation/radiation_band.cpp RadiationBandImpl::forward repo=pyharp >}}).
2. `DisortImpl::forward` checks the shapes against the configured wave and column counts and builds the iterator
   ({{< code src/disort.cpp DisortImpl::forward repo=pydisort >}}).
3. The dispatch stub picks `call_disort_cpu`, or on CUDA tensors `call_disort_cuda` if the installed library has it;
   otherwise torch raises `DispatchStub: missing kernel for cuda`.

### Tests

@tbl-ch09-disort-tests lists the checks.

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `check_ch09_batch_device.py` | DISORT batch against per-column calls, CPU | $10^{-14}$ (f64), $10^{-6}$ (f32) | one cdisort state per column |
| `check_ch09_batch_device.py` | CUDA against CPU, $\omega < 1$ columns | $10^{-12}$ (f64), @eq-ch09-toon-tol32 (f32) | as for Toon, @sec-ch09-toon |
| `check_ch09_batch_device.py` | CUDA against CPU, $\omega = 1$ columns | $10^{-9}$ (f64) | the amplified round-off of @eq-ch09-disort-dither |
| `check_ch09_matrix.py` | every cell present for both versions | complete | the matrix of @fig-ch09-disort-matrix |

: Tests of DISORT batching and dispatch. {#tbl-ch09-disort-tests}

Under pydisort 1.7.1 the check prints 72 lines with no failure: every DISORT and band call on CUDA is reported
`UNSUPPORTED` with the message `DispatchStub: missing kernel for cuda`, and every CPU comparison
passes.[^ch09-disort-171] Under pydisort 1.8.13 it prints 88 lines with no failure and 10 lines marked
`EXPECTED-FAIL`: the candidate defects of the Limits layer.[^ch09-disort-1813] On the CPU, DISORT gives
bit-identical fluxes under the two versions on the grid of the solver-comparison chapter, @sec-ch05.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- **No DISORT on CUDA with pydisort 1.7.1.** A band with `solver: disort` on CUDA tensors raises
  `DispatchStub: missing kernel for cuda`. pyharp's CI installs exactly this version.
- **Candidate defect: pydisort 1.8.13 on CUDA at 8 streams.** At `nstr` 8, CUDA differs from the CPU by
  $8.3\times10^{-5}$ (shortwave) and $2.9\times10^{-6}$ (thermal) in float64; in float32 the $\omega = 1$ columns
  are wrong by $6.2\times10^{4}$ and $5.8\times10^{8}$ times the largest flux, while staying finite. In version 1.8.13
  pydisort solves 4- and 8-stream flux-only problems on CUDA by a reduced "fast flux" path and sends $\omega = 1$
  columns to its general solver; the defect is confined to 8 streams. That version is not the pin of this report,
  so its code is described here and not cited; the measurement is the evidence.[^ch09-disort-1813]
- **Candidate defect: thermal $\omega = 1$ columns on CUDA, pydisort 1.8.13.** In float64 they differ from the CPU
  by $7\times10^{-8}$ to $1.1\times10^{-7}$ at every stream count, against $1.6\times10^{-13}$ for the other
  columns of the same runs. The cause is not measured.
- Both are one run on one GPU; they stay candidates until a second, independent run agrees.
- **Not measured.** Stream counts above 32 on CUDA, intensities (`onlyfl` off), timing on CUDA, and other GPUs.
:::
